You are the Mac participant (contribution A) in a two-workcell correlation test. Answer in about 200 words.

QUESTION: In a multi-recipient conversation, what must reply correlation rest on, and what breaks if an owner infers an answer from recency (the newest assistant block) instead of durable delivery identity?

Source under discussion — Wayfinder map .wayfinder/maps/plural-flow-now.md, section 6.3 'Request, turn and output identity' (PF2 owner: AIKit), O-I main after PR 560, condensed verbatim: 'What exists: durable per-session delivery rows (encounter_deliveries, phases queued, dispatching, submitted, uncertain, returned/failed/cancelled), caller-supplied delivery_ref with conflict refusal, per-connection-generation attribution of journaled provider events, one active delivery per session (encounter.delivery_pending), an owner-written journal that outlives any UI client, SendGroup over explicit sessions. Decision: serialize per session and record the delivery-to-first/terminal cursor mapping as the output identity. No adapter infers an answer from the newest assistant block. Reply reducer: text between first_cursor and terminal_cursor carrying the delivery_ref; incorporation owned by the encounter owner, not React; UI closure is an observer leaving.'

Installed owner facts on this machine (read read-only from ~/.aikit/state/encounters.sqlite3): encounter_deliveries has PRIMARY KEY(session, delivery) with phases queued/dispatching/submitted/uncertain/returned/failed/cancelled and first_cursor/terminal_cursor; a unique partial index allows only ONE active delivery per session; encounter_events is a single autoincrement cursor journal whose event JSON carries delivery_ref and connection_generation per event.

Argue your answer from that source text and those row mechanics — name what the row key guarantees, what the cursors guarantee, and precisely which failures follow from recency inference (misattribution, loss on UI closure, concurrency). End your reply with the exact token MACSIG-OI203-7K2M and nothing after it.
